case_title: TAIJUDDIN v. STATE OF ASSAM & ORS.
trial_court_outcome: Convicted and sentenced to life imprisonment
high_court_outcome: Convicted some while gave benefit of doubt to others
neutral_facts: A land dispute led to the death of the victim. A mob of accused persons approached the victim's house armed with weapons such as lathis, spears, and daggers. The victim attempted to escape by taking shelter in another house but was eventually surrounded, and the house was broken into. The victim was assaulted and his body was disposed of by being thrown into the river. The accused were charged with various offenses, and the trial court convicted all 32 accused and sentenced them to life imprisonment. The High Court upheld some convictions but gave a benefit of doubt to others. The accused in this case was alleged to have pointed out the location of the victim, but his presence at the scene was explained by the proximity of his house to the victim's hiding place. He was not found to have assaulted anyone or carried a weapon, and his involvement was not conclusively proven.
